meta.description: Omo River floodplain, 350–700m. High sedimentation, Gibe III context.

data_sources.soil: SoilGrids v2.0 — ISRIC REST API (shallowest depth ~0-5cm)
data_sources.dem: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 100m EPSG:32637 — Planetary Computer
data_sources.modis_lpi: MODIS MOD13Q1 v061 250m EPSG:32637 — Planetary Computer
data_sources.chirps: CHIRPS v2.0 2014–2023 annual TIFs — CHC UCSB /vsicurl/
data_sources.era5: ERA5-Land 2023 via Open-Meteo historical-forecast-api (free, no credentials)

community_intelligence.community_preferred_future: Sustainable irrigation without losing flooding benefits; reduce sedimentation; maintain fish access
community_intelligence.local_degradation_memory: Omo River flooding patterns changed after Gibe III (2016); siltation increasing; flood-recession agriculture disrupted
community_intelligence.grazing_rules: Seasonal riverine grazing by Hamar and Daasanach; riparian gallery forest has traditional protection
community_intelligence.labor_constraints: Irrigation scheme maintenance requires labor often unavailable in dry season
community_intelligence.gendered_burdens: Women fish, collect riverine plants, and manage household water from river
community_intelligence.youth_opportunities: Sediment monitoring technicians, irrigation maintenance, fish value chain development
community_intelligence.local_conflict_risks: EXTREMELY HIGH — Omo basin has documented violent conflicts; Gibe III dam displacement grievances unresolved
community_intelligence.tenure_constraints: Riverine land disputed between state irrigation schemes and traditional users
adoption_barriers: Gibe III dam operation beyond community control
